title: An LLM agent in an air-free robotic lab maps lithium halide spinel conductors
summary: An agent-guided self-driving lab ran 352 air-sensitive synthesis samples, realizing 72% of the 171 pairwise combinations of 19 metals. The share of samples meeting both ionic conductivity above 0.05 mS/cm and high spinel phase purity rose from 1.33% in the first 75 agent-proposed samples to 5.33% in the last 75. This is an arXiv preprint; characterization methods and new-compound counts are not confirmed from the abstract page.
ai_technology: A-Lab GPSS (LLM agent integrated into a robotic synthesis platform)
organization: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and University of California, Berkeley

evidence.tested: A robotic air-free platform synthesized and characterized 352 spinel samples; the share meeting conductivity and phase-purity criteria was compared between the first and last 75 agent-proposed samples.
evidence.unknown: The abstract states no limitations, does not describe the measurement methods, and shows no scalability beyond this campaign.
evidence.ai_role: An agentic AI framework using abductive and inductive reasoning structured the autonomous experimental design.
